definition: the treatment of disease, especially cancer, using controlled doses of radiation.

collocations.example: She had to undergo radiotherapy for several weeks after the surgery.
The doctor recommended a full course of radiotherapy to shrink the tumor.

definition: a colorless radioactive gas that occurs naturally and can be harmful in buildings.

collocations.example: High levels of radon gas were detected in the basement.
Home inspectors often test for radon before a sale closes.

definition: a wide bank of earth or a stone wall built to protect a castle or city.

collocations.example: Soldiers stood ready to defend the ramparts against the attack.
Guards patrolled atop the rampart through the night.

definition: badly built or in bad condition and likely to fall apart.

collocations.example: They lived in a ramshackle building at the edge of town.
The old barn had come to look ramshackle after years of neglect.

definition: to search a place roughly and carelessly, often causing damage or stealing things.

collocations.example: Burglars ransacked the house while the family was away for the weekend.
He ransacked the office looking for the signed contract.

definition: so interested in something that you do not notice anything else.

collocations.example: The children listened to the story with rapt attention.
She was completely rapt in the music and heard nothing else.

definition: to put the parts of something back together after it has been taken apart.

collocations.example: After cleaning, he reassembled the parts of the engine.
We had to take the bookshelf apart and reassemble it upstairs.

definition: refusing to obey or cooperate, even after being asked many times.

collocations.example: Teachers struggled to manage the recalcitrant child in class.
Several members proved recalcitrant and blocked every proposal.

definition: to repeat the main points of something that has been said or decided.

collocations.example: Let me recap the main points before we end the meeting.
To recap briefly, the project will launch next spring.

definition: to change the form or structure of something so it is different.

collocations.example: The lecture was recast as a short radio program.
Management recast the plan to focus on smaller markets.

definition: an angry statement accusing someone, especially in reply to a similar accusation.

collocations.example: The meeting ended in mutual recrimination and blame.
They agreed to part ways without recrimination.

definition: the house where a rector or parish priest lives.

collocations.example: They bought the old rectory and turned it into a home.
The new priest will live in the rectory next to the church.

definition: to replace an existing loan with a new one, usually at better terms.

collocations.example: The company took out a new loan to refinance its existing debt.
Homeowners rushed to refinance at a lower rate last year.

definition: a person who rules a country when the king or queen is too young or unable to rule.

collocations.example: The dying king appointed his brother as regent for the young prince.
His mother acted as regent until he came of age.

definition: to be born again in another body after death, according to some beliefs.

collocations.example: Some believe a person can be reincarnated as an animal.
According to the faith, people reincarnate after death into a new life.

definition: to break a promise or fail to do what you agreed to do.

collocations.example: He reneged on his promise to help pay for the trip.
She feared he would later renege and leave them stranded.

definition: filled or well supplied with something.

collocations.example: The report was replete with useful charts.
They sat at a table replete with fresh fruit.

definition: causing a strong feeling of dislike or disgust.

collocations.example: Many found the policy morally repugnant and refused to support it.
The very idea of cheating was repugnant to her.

definition: so unpleasant that it makes you feel sick or strongly dislike it.

collocations.example: Most visitors found the smell in the alley repulsive.
The rotting food was a repulsive sight on the counter.

definition: a piece of music or a church service held in memory of a dead person.

collocations.example: The family attended a requiem mass for their grandfather.
The composer wrote a requiem in honor of the war dead.

definition: the process of breathing air in and out of the lungs.

collocations.example: The lifeguard performed artificial respiration on the swimmer.
The nurse recorded the patient's respiration rate every hour.

definition: to make a tape or recording go back to an earlier point.

collocations.example: He rewound the tape to watch the scene again.
She liked to rewind and replay her favorite songs.

definition: relating to a disease that causes painful swelling in the joints.

collocations.example: Her grandmother suffers from rheumatoid arthritis in her hands.
The blood test checks for rheumatoid factor in the body.

definition: a large bush with bright flowers and leaves that stay green all year.

collocations.example: A huge rhododendron bush bloomed beside the garden gate.
A bank of rhododendrons lined the woodland walk.

definition: a plant with long red stems that are cooked and eaten as a fruit.

collocations.example: She baked a sweet rhubarb pie for dessert.
We had stewed rhubarb with custard after lunch.

definition: weak and likely to break or fall, especially furniture or structures.

collocations.example: She hurried up the rickety staircase to the top floor.
The old pier looked rickety after years of storms.

definition: built in a style of architecture with round arches, common in medieval Europe.

collocations.example: The cathedral is a fine example of Romanesque architecture.
The abbey was built in the Romanesque style.

definition: a string of beads used by Catholics for counting prayers.

collocations.example: Every evening she would say the rosary before bed.
He held a worn string of rosary beads in his hand.

definition: a round decoration shaped like a rose, often made of ribbon.

collocations.example: Her pony won a blue rosette at the local show.
A ribbon rosette was pinned to the winner's jacket.

definition: a large, strong breed of dog often used as a guard dog.

collocations.example: It takes patience to train a rottweiler properly.
They adopted a rottweiler puppy from the shelter.

definition: a set of instructions or rules, especially a guide for scoring work.

collocations.example: The teacher graded the essays using a scoring rubric.
The teacher graded essays using a detailed grading rubric.

definition: a bag with shoulder straps carried on the back.

collocations.example: He carried a heavy backpack on the long hike.
He set off with a backpack on his back.

definition: a stiff, frilled collar worn around the neck, popular in the 1500s.

collocations.example: In the portrait he wears an elaborate ruff.
A delicate lace ruff encircled her throat.

definition: to make something messy or full of folds and wrinkles.

collocations.example: She leaned over to rumple the little boy's hair.
He rumpled up the letter and threw it away.

definition: the unit of money used in India, Pakistan, and some other countries.

collocations.example: The Indian rupee fell against the dollar last week.
The snack cost only a few rupees at the stall.

definition: a bright yellow-orange spice used to color and flavor food.

collocations.example: She added a pinch of saffron to the rice.
The recipe calls for a few saffron threads soaked in water.

definition: a type of hard, spicy sausage, usually eaten in thin slices.

collocations.example: He put a slice of salami on the sandwich.
They served salami and cheese with crackers.

definition: a type of bacteria in food that can cause serious food poisoning.

collocations.example: Several diners came down with salmonella poisoning.
The eggs were found to be contaminated with salmonella.

definition: a small collection of different things meant to show or try a range.

collocations.example: We ordered the sampler platter to try several dishes.
The album is a sampler of her early work.

definition: to make something holy or free from sin.

collocations.example: The priest performed a rite to sanctify the new chapel.
The ground was sanctified by an ancient blessing.

definition: cheerful and confident that things will turn out well.

collocations.example: She remained sanguine about the team's chances.
He took a sanguine view of the economy's future.

definition: without (used in a humorous or stylish way).

collocations.example: She showed up to the photo shoot sans makeup.
He ordered a burger sans the bun to cut carbs.

definition: a young tree.

collocations.example: Volunteers planted saplings along the riverbank.
A slender sapling grew at the forest's edge.

definition: having practical knowledge and good judgment about something.

collocations.example: Young, tech-savvy workers adapted quickly to the new tools.
A savvy investor spreads risk across many assets.

definition: a hard, dry crust that forms over a cut or wound as it heals.

collocations.example: The cut will form a scab within a day or two.
The doctor told him not to pick at the scab.

definition: a small, very sharp knife used by surgeons in operations.

collocations.example: The surgeon's scalpel made a clean, precise cut.
The doctor wielded the scalpel with steady hands.

definition: a strong disagreement that splits a group into opposing sides.

collocations.example: The dispute caused a deep schism within the party.
A schism between the two factions divided the church.

definition: a small, round baked bread, often eaten with butter or jam.

collocations.example: She enjoyed a warm, buttered scone with her tea.
He baked a batch of scones for breakfast.

definition: equipment that lets a diver breathe underwater.

collocations.example: He learned to scuba dive on vacation in Thailand.
All the scuba gear is stored in the shed by the dock.

definition: to move quickly and smoothly, driven by the wind.

collocations.example: Dark clouds scudded across the sky before the storm.
The small boat scudded before the wind toward the harbor.

definition: to scrape or mark a surface by rubbing it roughly.

collocations.example: He scuffed his new shoes on the rough pavement.
The movers scuffed up the hardwood floors.

definition: a car with a closed body and a separate trunk, seating four or more.

collocations.example: They arrived in a sleek luxury sedan.
She drives a small sedan to work each day.

definition: dirty, unpleasant, and possibly involving illegal or immoral activity.

collocations.example: They met in a seedy bar on the edge of town.
The whole neighborhood looked seedy and run-down.

definition: the fluid produced by male sex organs that contains sperm.

collocations.example: Diet can affect a man's semen quality.
The clinic collected a sample of semen for testing.

definition: one of the two main periods that a school or college year is divided into.

collocations.example: She is taking five classes in the fall semester.
Students must complete three essays during the semester.

definition: relating to signs and symbols and how they create meaning.

collocations.example: Language is a complex semiotic system.
From a semiotic perspective, colors carry cultural meaning.

definition: losing mental abilities, especially memory, because of old age.

collocations.example: His family worried that he was going senile.
She was diagnosed with senile dementia.

definition: to make someone more aware of or sensitive to something.

collocations.example: The campaign aims to sensitize people to the issue of poverty.
Through training, staff became sensitized to customers' needs.

definition: a person or thing that keeps watch or stands guard.

collocations.example: Tall pines stood sentinel along the old road.
A lone sentinel guarded the castle gate.

definition: infected with harmful bacteria.

collocations.example: The untreated wound went septic within days.
The doctor cleaned the septic wound carefully.

definition: the clear liquid part of blood, used in medical tests and treatments.

collocations.example: The lab analyzed the patient's blood serum.
Technicians test the serum for signs of infection.

definition: a chemical in the brain that affects mood, sleep, and emotions.

collocations.example: Exercise can raise serotonin levels in the brain.
Certain foods are said to boost serotonin naturally.

definition: a thick, deep pile on a carpet or rug.

collocations.example: The basement still had an orange shag carpet from the seventies.
The living room was covered in a soft, deep-pile shag.

definition: a title for the former kings of Iran.

collocations.example: The shah of Iran fled the country in 1979.
The economy changed greatly under the shah.

definition: a small, roughly built hut or shack, usually in a poor area.

collocations.example: Thousands of people live in the shanty town outside the city.
The family crowded into a small tin-roofed shanty.

definition: a bundle of things tied together, such as papers or cut stalks of grain.

collocations.example: She carried a thick sheaf of papers into the meeting.
Workers gathered the cut grain into sheaves.

definition: to put a sword or knife into its cover.

collocations.example: The warrior sheathed his sword after the battle ended.
He quickly sheathed his weapon when the alarm stopped.

definition: to move back or avoid something suddenly because of fear or dislike.

collocations.example: She tends to shy away from large crowds.
He would never shy from a tough decision.

definition: badly made or done, using poor materials or little care.

collocations.example: The house was full of shoddy workmanship.
The cheap repair job looked shoddy.

definition: a quicker way to get somewhere or to achieve something.

collocations.example: We took a shortcut across the field to save time.
There is no shortcut to real success.

definition: a long piece of furniture for storing dishes, with a flat top for serving.

collocations.example: Plates were displayed on the mahogany sideboard.
She set the dishes on the sideboard before dinner.

definition: to walk toward or away from someone in a quiet, careful way.

collocations.example: A stranger sidled up to us and asked for money.
He sidled away before anyone could speak to him.

definition: a hard, white or colorless mineral found in sand and used to make glass.

collocations.example: A packet of silica gel keeps the box dry.
The volcanic rock is high in silica.

definition: a mathematical ratio in a right triangle, relating an angle to its opposite side.

collocations.example: The sine of a thirty-degree angle is one half.
The signal forms a smooth sine wave on the screen.

definition: a strong band of tissue that connects muscle to bone.

collocations.example: Years of labor had built up his muscle and sinew.
The meat was full of tough sinew.

definition: to move liquid from one container to another through a tube.

collocations.example: They used a hose to siphon off the water.
Someone tried to siphon gas from the parked car.

definition: giving only a few details and not thorough or complete.

collocations.example: Police released only sketchy details of the crash.
Information about the cause remains sketchy.

definition: waste material left after metal is separated from rock by melting.

collocations.example: Molten slag poured from the furnace.
Workers remove the slag from the surface of the metal.

definition: dishonest or immoral behavior, especially in politics or business.

collocations.example: The minister faced new allegations of sleaze.
Voters were tired of corruption and sleaze in government.

definition: a small vehicle on runners for sliding over snow.

collocations.example: The dogs pulled the sled across the frozen lake.
The children rode on a sled down the snowy hill.

definition: a mix of rain and snow, or rain that freezes as it falls.

collocations.example: They walked home through the driving sleet.
The rain turned to sleet as the temperature dropped.

definition: a thin, watery mixture of a fine solid, such as cement or mud.

collocations.example: Workers poured the cement slurry into the mold.
Mix the powder with water until the clay forms a thick slurry.

definition: to feel a sharp, stinging pain.

collocations.example: The thick smoke made her eyes smart.
His cheek still smarted from the slap.

definition: to hit someone or something hard, especially in battle (old use).

collocations.example: The warrior rose up to smite the enemy.
Legend says the god would smite down the wicked.

definition: a small piece of something, especially information, text, or code.

collocations.example: She shared a useful snippet of information.
He pasted a short code snippet into the chat.

definition: to look around a place secretly to find private information.

collocations.example: He caught someone snooping around his office.
The app was accused of snooping on its users.

definition: the long nose and mouth of an animal such as a pig or dog.

collocations.example: The pig pushed its snout into the mud.
The animal has a long snout for sniffing out food.

definition: completely wet, soaked through with water.

collocations.example: They peeled off their sodden clothes by the fire.
The field was sodden with rain after the storm.

definition: a short stay in a place, away from home.

collocations.example: After a brief sojourn in Paris, she returned home.
He learned the language during his sojourn abroad.

definition: a roll in which you turn your whole body forward or backward.

collocations.example: The gymnast did a perfect somersault.
He landed the backward somersault with ease.

definition: a piece of classical music for one or two instruments, in several parts.

collocations.example: She played a Beethoven piano sonata.
The young musician composed her first sonata.

definition: unwanted email sent to many people, usually advertising something.

collocations.example: Filters block most email spam before it arrives.
The spam filter caught the suspicious message.

definition: the study of how light is absorbed or given off by substances, used to identify them.

collocations.example: Infrared spectroscopy revealed the structure of the molecule.
Scientists use spectroscopy to study distant stars.

definition: a thin rod used for spinning and twisting thread by hand or machine.

collocations.example: She turned the spindle to twist the wool into yarn.
The old spinning wheel had a worn wooden spindle.

definition: an older woman who has never married (now often considered old-fashioned).

collocations.example: She was often described as an old spinster.
She chose to remain a spinster all her life.

definition: to spread out or turn outward, especially fingers or legs.

collocations.example: His fingers splayed out across the table.
The frog splays its legs when it jumps.

definition: an organ near the stomach that helps clean the blood and fight infection.

collocations.example: The accident left him with a ruptured spleen.
Surgeons had to remove the damaged spleen.

definition: one of the thin rods that connect the center of a wheel to its rim.

collocations.example: A broken spoke made the bicycle wheel wobble.
Her coat caught in the spokes of the wheel.
